EnableBackpackLightsTrack.blurb: When true, animation backpack-light keyframes are actually sent from the anim process to the robot hardware. When false (default), those keyframes are dropped even if the backpack track is unlocked — so canned animations do not drive the backpack LEDs through the animation streamer path.
EnableBackpackLightsTrack.detail: Checked in AnimationStreamer::SendIfTrackUnlocked for BACKPACK_LIGHTS_TRACK only. Head/lift/body tracks do not use this flag. The backpack track is still often locked separately (_lockedTracks starts with backpack locked; shipping builds force it locked). This console var is an extra gate on top of unlock: both unlock and EnableBackpackLightsTrack true are needed for animation backpack frames to reach the robot. Procedural/engine backpack light APIs are separate systems.
EnableBackpackLightsTrack.howTo: 1) Unlock the backpack lights track if your build allows it (ANKI_DEV_CHEATS). 2) Set EnableBackpackLightsTrack true. 3) Play an animation that has backpack light keyframes and watch the backpack LEDs.

EnableHeadProceduralMovement.blurb: Master switch for procedural head motor sound. When true, Vector’s audio engine plays a head movement loop and updates head speed/acceleration parameters from live robot state. When false (default), no procedural head SFX are started or updated.
EnableHeadProceduralMovement.detail: ProceduralAudioClient listens to RobotToEngine state messages (after syncRobotAck). UpdateHeadState returns immediately if this flag is false. This does not change actual head motor commands — only the synthetic “servo whir” style loops (Play/Stop Robot_Vic_Sfx Head_Loop and RTPCs Robot_Vic_Head_Speed / Head_Accelerate). Head is off by default; lift and treads default on.

EnableLiftProceduralMovement.blurb: Master switch for procedural lift (fork) motor sound. When true (default), lift motion triggers a lift loop SFX with speed/acceleration RTPCs. When false, lift motion is silent on this procedural path.
EnableLiftProceduralMovement.detail: Same architecture as head/tread: state-driven loops via Wwise GameObject Procedural, events Play/Stop Robot_Vic_Sfx Lift_Loop, parameters Robot_Vic_Lift_Speed and Lift_Accelerate. Does not move the lift — only sound. Default true so production freeplay includes lift motor audio.

EnablePausePrams.blurb: When true (default), text-to-speech applies the silence/pause console timings (leading/trailing silence and punctuation/comma/etc. pauses) to each new Acapela utterance. When false, those pause parameters are not written into the TTS engine — speech uses Acapela’s default pause behavior instead. Name is a historical typo for “Params,” not prams/strollers.
EnablePausePrams.detail: TextToSpeechProviderConfig::GetEnablePauseParams returns this flag. On the robot (VICOS), GetFirstAudioData only SETs BABIL_PARM_LEADINGSILENCE, TRAILINGSILENCE, and PAUSE1–5SILENCE when the flag is true. Comment in code: if you set any of those, the rest also need to be set — this flag batches them. Does not re-synthesize already prepared waves; next GetFirstAudioData only. Spelling of dump id is EnablePausePrams (missing “a” in Params).

EnableTreadProceduralMovement.blurb: Master switch for procedural tread/drive motor sound. When true (default), wheel motion starts a tread loop SFX with speed, acceleration, and spin RTPCs. When false, driving is silent on this procedural path.
EnableTreadProceduralMovement.detail: UpdateTreadState early-outs when false. Detects point-turn vs drive using left/right wheel speeds and feeds Robot_Vic_Tread_Speed, Tread_Accelerate, and Tread_Spin_Speed. Spin RTPC > 0 means “point turn”; near-zero default (−0.01) means straight/curve drive. Sound only — does not change driving.

GlitchLightDelay_ms.blurb: Intended delay (ms) before a backpack “glitch” light sequence would start flashing. Default 200. Currently has no effect: the glitch light generator body is commented out.
GlitchLightDelay_ms.detail: Registered under category GlitchLights and only referenced inside a large block comment in BackpackLayerManager::GenerateGlitchLights. That function still runs (from TrackLayerComponent::AddGlitch) but only clears the track; the keyframes that used delay/duration are disabled. Code notes TODO VIC-447 restore glitching. Changing this var does not alter backpack LEDs until that path is restored.
GlitchLightDelay_ms.statusNote: Only live uses are inside a multi-line comment; GenerateGlitchLights clears the track and does not schedule frames.

GlitchLightDuration_ms.blurb: Intended duration (ms) of each step in a backpack glitch light sequence. Default 60. Currently has no effect for the same reason as GlitchLightDelay_ms — generation code is commented out.
GlitchLightDuration_ms.detail: Would have timed successive red backpack LED flashes (middle, then random sides) after GlitchLightDelay_ms. All of that logic is wrapped in /* … */ inside GenerateGlitchLights. AddGlitch still calls the function for face distortion and an empty backpack layer.
GlitchLightDuration_ms.statusNote: Registered and named in dump, but only referenced inside commented-out glitch keyframe construction.

HeadCoolDown_ms.blurb: After procedural head motor sound stops, how long (ms) the system waits before allowing the head loop to start again. Default 65; console range 0–250. Reduces rapid stop/start chatter when the head jitters near the movement threshold.
HeadCoolDown_ms.detail: On transition to Stopped, ProceduralAudioClient sets _headCoolDownExpiresTimeStamp_ms = now + this value. While in cooldown, a new move goes to PendingStart instead of Started (no Play event until cooldown ends and still moving). Only matters when EnableHeadProceduralMovement is true.

HeadMovementThreshold_rpms.blurb: Minimum absolute head angular speed (radians per millisecond) counted as “moving” for procedural head audio. Default 0.0 so any nonzero computed speed counts; range 0–0.01.
HeadMovementThreshold_rpms.detail: AudioProceduralFrame::IsHeadMoving compares |headSpeed_rpms| to this threshold. Head speed is delta headAngle_rad / delta time_ms from consecutive RobotState samples. Raising this ignores tiny head drifts so the head SFX loop does not trip on sensor noise. Used only for start/stop of the loop, not for RTPC magnitude (that uses MaxHeadSpeed_rpms).

LiftCoolDown_ms.blurb: Cooldown (ms) after procedural lift sound stops before a new lift loop may start. Default 65; range 0–250.
LiftCoolDown_ms.detail: Same FrameStateUpdate cooldown pattern as head/treads. Applied when EnableLiftProceduralMovement is true. Stops micro-chatter if lift angle noise crosses the movement threshold.

LiftMovementThreshold_rpms.blurb: Minimum absolute lift angular speed (rad/ms) treated as lift motion for procedural audio. Default 0.0; range 0–0.01.
LiftMovementThreshold_rpms.detail: IsLiftMoving uses |liftSpeed_rpms| > threshold. Lift speed is derived from consecutive liftAngle samples. Higher values require more decisive lift motion before the lift loop plays.

MaxHeadAccel_rpms2.blurb: Scale reference for head angular acceleration fed into the procedural audio RTPC (normalized −1…1). Default 0.0001 rad/ms²; range 0–0.001. Larger values make the same physical accel sound “milder” (lower |RTPC|).
MaxHeadAccel_rpms2.detail: GetNormalizedHeadAcceleration = clamp(headAccel / this, −1, 1), then sign-flipped when head speed is negative so accel RTPC tracks direction of travel. headAccel is Δspeed/Δt between frames. Only affects Robot_Vic_Head_Accelerate while the head loop is active.

MaxHeadSpeed_rpms.blurb: Full-scale head angular speed for procedural audio: normalized head speed RTPC = clamp(actual / this, −1…1). Default 0.005 rad/ms; range 0–0.025. Smaller max makes moderate head moves sound “faster” in the mix.
MaxHeadSpeed_rpms.detail: Does not limit real head motors. Units are radians per millisecond from angle deltas on RobotState. Sign encodes up vs down. Pushed as Robot_Vic_Head_Speed when setRTPC is true.

MaxLiftAccel_rpms2.blurb: Full-scale lift acceleration for procedural audio normalization (−1…1 RTPC). Default 0.0001 rad/ms²; range 0–0.001.
MaxLiftAccel_rpms2.detail: Same pattern as head: clamp(accel/max), sign with lift speed direction → Robot_Vic_Lift_Accelerate. Audio-only scale, not a hardware limit.

MaxLiftSpeed_rpms.blurb: Full-scale lift angular speed for procedural audio RTPC. Default 0.0025 rad/ms; range 0–0.05. Normalized lift speed = clamp(actual / this, −1…1).
MaxLiftSpeed_rpms.detail: Maps to Robot_Vic_Lift_Speed. Raising the max softens the perceived lift motor intensity for a given motion; lowering exaggerates it. Does not cap real lift velocity.

MaxTreadAccel_mmpms2.blurb: Full-scale tread (drive) acceleration for procedural audio. Default 5.0 mm/ms²; range 0–10. Normalized accel RTPC is clamped to −1…1 against this scale, with sign following average tread speed direction.
MaxTreadAccel_mmpms2.detail: Tread accel is Δ(avg wheel speed)/Δt. Parameter Robot_Vic_Tread_Accelerate. Audio-only; not a chassis control limit.

MaxTreadSpeed_mmps.blurb: Full-scale average wheel speed for procedural tread drive sound. Default equals MAX_WHEEL_SPEED_MMPS (220 mm/s); console range about 120–320 (±100 around that constant). Normalized tread speed RTPC = avgWheelSpeed / this.
MaxTreadSpeed_mmps.detail: Average of left and right wheel speeds from RobotState. Can exceed ±1.0 if wheels exceed this scale (unlike head/lift which clamp). Point-turn intensity uses MaxTurnSpeed_mmps separately via spin RTPC. Does not limit real driving speed.

MaxTurnSpeed_mmps.blurb: Full-scale differential (spin) speed for procedural point-turn audio. Default 220 mm/s (same MAX_WHEEL_SPEED_MMPS); range about 120–320. Normalized turn = min(|left−right| / this, 1).
MaxTurnSpeed_mmps.detail: When |turnSpeed| is larger than both the max and |min| wheel speeds, the client treats the motion as a point turn and sets Robot_Vic_Tread_Spin_Speed to the normalized value; otherwise spin RTPC stays slightly negative (−0.01) so the audio engine uses tread speed instead. Audio-only scale.

TreadCoolDown_ms.blurb: Cooldown (ms) after procedural tread sound stops before a new tread loop may start. Default 65; range 0–250.
TreadCoolDown_ms.detail: Set when tread frame state becomes Stopped. During cooldown, renewed motion is PendingStart until the timer expires. Prevents rapid loop restarts on stop-and-go driving. Requires EnableTreadProceduralMovement.

TreadMovementThreshold_mmps.blurb: Minimum absolute left or right wheel speed (mm/s) that counts as “treads moving” for procedural drive audio. Default 0.0; range 0–0.01.
TreadMovementThreshold_mmps.detail: IsTreadMoving is true if either wheel exceeds this threshold. With default 0, any nonzero wheel report starts/stops the loop logic. Slight increases reject tiny residual wheel reports without needing a large deadband.
